title: Denver Broncos Work Out 3 Versatile Veteran Linebackers on Friday
description: The Denver Broncos might not be done addressing their linebacker and special teams depth if Friday's tryouts are any indication. The post Denver Broncos Work Out 3 Versatile Veteran Linebackers on Friday appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Denver Broncos might not be done addressing the linebacker depth. Three days after they worked out four players (including two linebackers), they again kicked the tires on three 'backers on Friday.

Per the NFL's official transaction wire, they had veterans Cameron Goode, Elliott Brown, and Jahfari Harvey in for tryouts today.

Harvey and Brown both joined the league as undrafted free agents in 2025. Harvey was signed to the Raiders' practice squad (as a defensive end) last season and was called up to compete in two games. He was also re-signed to the practice squad last week but got cut a few days later.

Brown actually began his career in the CFL with the Edmonton Elks in 2023. He stood out from the crowd there (earning CFL West All-Star honors in 2024) over the next two seasons and spent much of last season on the Cardinals' practice squad.

Meanwhile, Goode was drafted by the Dolphins in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He's played in 37 games in Miami, starting two of them, over his first three years. He didn't survive the Dolphins' final roster cuts last week.

Goode might not be a big name, but he's been a key member of the Dolphins' special teams unit since joining the league. He has played 678 snaps in the third phase throughout his career, including 309 snaps (68% of their total special teams snaps) as a rookie and 318 snaps (73%) last season.

Denver Gazette's Chris Tomasson also highlighted Goode, who also has 196 career defensive snaps under his belt, as the most intriguing tryout player.

"Goode is the most notable of the three. He played in 37 games the past three seasons with Miami, with one start. Got in for 14 defensive snaps in Dolphins' infamous 70-20 win over #Broncos in Week 3 in 2023." Tomasson wrote on X.

There is a clear theme among the seven players the Broncos have worked out this week. They're not exactly shopping in the used car section for veterans that could help them on defense (which isn't a surprise, considering how much talent they have on the defensive side of the ball).

Their depth at linebacker is somewhat of a question mark, but they conceivably should feel good about what Red Murdock showed in the preseason in that regard. They could call him up from the practice squad in a pinch if injuries strike.

The players that they've kicked the tires on have three career starts between all seven of them. Most of them do bring special teams experience, though. That could be an area where the Broncos are looking for reinforcements.

They opted not to even bring back undrafted rookie linebacker Taurean York, who also showed some promise on the defensive side of the ball, to the practice squad. Their lack of interest there could be partially due to him struggling in the third phase throughout preseason.

Special teams are an underrated aspect when it comes to team construction. The Broncos might not feel confident in the depth they have in the special teams room (aside from Marvin Mims Jr. providing an elite impact in the return game). That would explain the under-the-radar players they've been looking into.

title: “Stay Safe”: ESPN’s Laura Rutledge Gives Alarming Update for Texas-Ohio State Game as Calls Mount for Longhorns to Make Big Change
description: Texas and Ohio State already have enough going on Saturday. No.
fullText:
Texas and Ohio State already have enough going on Saturday. No. 1 vs. No. 4, a packed house, and national attention. But fans are going to have to face another tough opponent. When ESPN's Laura Rutledge got to Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, she realized the heat was going to be part of the story.

"Look at this gorgeous place," Laura Rutledge said while showing the stadium. "It is extremely hot. Now, game time is going to be a little later than it is right now, but I think we're looking at about 100 degrees of kickoff tomorrow."

A fan of hers commented on the video,

"Laura, have fun tomorrow at the Texas vs Ohio State game in Austin,Texas and drink enough water Laura to stay hydrated please and thank you ???? stay safe and have fun at Austin,Texas tomorrow for the college football ???? game."

Texas Ohio State is going to be electric, but the Austin heat is a character of its own. 

Saturday's forecast calls for temperatures around 102 degrees, with the heat index potentially pushing above 100. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for areas along and east of Interstate 35 from noon through 7 p.m. The kickoff is at 6:30 p.m.

Texas fans have already learned what that kind of afternoon can feel like. The season opener against Texas State was played at 2:30 p.m., with temperatures reaching 102 degrees and a heat index of 105. Austin-Travis County EMS transported 13 people from the stadium to hospitals, with three cases potentially heat-related. That experience left plenty of fans unimpressed with the idea of doing it all over again.

UT graduate student Alaiza Mata said she almost passed out. Another recalled people vomiting nearby and said some fans couldn't make it through the first half. Still, another student described the sun as something beyond ordinary Austin summer heat. Those stories are why Laura Rutledge's warning is getting attention before an even bigger crowd arrives. But the warning does not stop with the air temperature.

As Laura Rutledge noted, field temperatures at the stadium's artificial surface have reportedly climbed to roughly 160 degrees Fahrenheit during the hottest part of the day. That number opened a debate among Longhorn fans. Why is Texas still playing on synthetic turf?

One frustrated supporter wrote, "There is no good reason for Texas to have synthetic turf. A former Texas AD once arrogantly let us know they have more money than the Vatican. It should be mandatory as a member of the SEC to have all outdoor athletic facilities be natural grass." That argument probably was not going away after the turf-temperature report.

Another fan took a different approach, threatening to give up the seats rather than battle the weather again. "You're seriously making me consider selling my tix. Now taking bids. 2 seats on the 20 yd down low," they posted.

Then came the inevitable internet joke about cooking temperatures. "Isn't 160 a 'well done' cooking safe temp," one fan asked.

Not everybody is running for the exits, though. Some fans remember that the opener was even worse. "Last week on the field was hotter UT vs. TXST," one wrote.

And another summed up the attitude of the faithful. "Place is going to be rocking even with such suppressive heat," they commented.

That is probably the safest bet of the weekend. Texas-Ohio State is not the kind of game that empties a stadium. Still, Austin-Travis County EMS has plenty of reason to be cautious. Fans are being encouraged to drink water before arriving and throughout the day, wear lightweight clothing, use sunscreen, limit alcohol and caffeine, and step into shade or air conditioning whenever possible.

Starting hydration Friday night instead of trying to catch up Saturday is also recommended. The football will eventually take center stage. But Saturday begins with a different question. Can everyone handle the heat before Texas and Ohio State handle each other?

title: Alexander Zverev says if he is actually looking forward to playing an American in the US Open final
description: Alexander Zverev will play Ben Shelton or Frances Tiafoe in the 2026 US Open men’s singles final. Playing the first of the two men’s semi-finals,...
fullText:
Alexander Zverev will play Ben Shelton or Frances Tiafoe in the 2026 US Open men's singles final.

Playing the first of the two men's semi-finals, Zverev defeated Karen Khachanov in straight sets.

During his post-match interview, the German said he planned to watch the second semi-final between the two Americans.

Then, in his press conference, Zverev was asked to comment on the prospect of playing an American in the US Open final.

"I enjoy these kinds of atmospheres," said Zverev.

"I've played a lot of French guys in France. I think the most hostile crowd, if you call it that, is if you're playing a French player in Paris, Bercy, back in the day. That was quite intense, and I always enjoyed those kinds of atmospheres.

"Of course I've played Australian guys in Australia, played Arthur Fery now in Wimbledon. The Wimbledon crowd is a bit different, though; there is no question about that!

"But for me, a loud and energetic crowd is always great, as long as they are fair.

"As long as they don't interrupt in the middle of points.

"I always enjoy these kinds of atmospheres."

Zverev says he has no problems with hostile crowds, but does his record reflect that?

2-1 vs Australian players at the Australian Open

5-0 vs French players at the French Open

2-0 vs British players at Wimbledon

5-1 vs American players at the US Open

The German is a combined 14-2 against players competing at their home Grand Slams.

He did, however, lose the last time he played against an American at the US Open – to Taylor Fritz two years ago.

Zverev will be keen to avoid the same fate on Sunday.

The top seed will play Tiafoe or Shelton in the final.

Starting with Tiafoe, he shared his thoughts on both players during his press conference.

"Frances [Tiafoe] is somebody who can do anything with a tennis ball; he can be aggressive, he can also mess around with it a little bit," said Zverev.

"He can be tricky to play, for sure.

"I have massive respect for him.

"I've known him for almost 20 years now, similar to Karen."

Zverev described Tiafoe as 'tricky to play', although his head-to-head record tells a different story.

Alexander Zverev and Frances Tiafoe's head-to-head record

He has only lost to Tiafoe once, winning their nine other ATP Tour meetings.

Zverev also has a dominant head-to-head record against Shelton, but was keen to compliment the 23-year-old.

Alexander Zverev and Ben Shelton's head-to-head record

"Ben [Shelton] is just a big, powerful guy," he said.

"Massive serve, massive groundstrokes, everything he does is just big.

"They're different styles of tennis players, but they're both very exciting."

Zverev knows better than to underestimate his opponents, even if he will walk onto the court as the favourite to win the US Open.

The 2026 US Open men's singles final will be played on Sunday, September 13.

title: Greene has 3 hits and Dingler hits slump-breaking homer in Tigers' 6-2 win over Rockies
description: Riley Greene had three hits, Dillon Dingler homered and the Detroit Tigers beat the Colorado Rockies 6-2 on Friday night.  The Tigers have won three of four after a 5-17 skid that dropped them out of the American League wild-card race.  Colorado has lost eight straight road games, scoring just 17 runs during the streak.
fullText:
DETROIT (AP) — Riley Greene had three hits, Dillon Dingler homered and the Detroit Tigers beat the Colorado Rockies 6-2 on Friday night.

The Tigers have won three of four after a 5-17 skid that dropped them out of the American League wild-card race.

Colorado has lost eight straight road games, scoring just 17 runs during the streak.

Framber Valdez (10-10) picked up the win, allowing one unearned run on six hits and two walks in six innings. Valdez has won each of his last two starts, allowing zero earned runs in 13 innings. Kenley Jansen got the last out for his 19th save.

Rockies starter Mason Adams allowed one run on two hits and three walks in five innings, but the bullpen gave up four runs in the sixth.

Rookie Max Clark tied it for Detroit in the sixth with his third career homer.

The Tigers then scored four times in the sixth, aided by a well-timed ABS challenge from Greene.

With two out and a runner on first, plate umpire Ron Kulpa called Greene out on a 2-2 pitch, but it was overturned when Greene challenged. He fouled off three 3-2 fastballs from Mark Manfredi (1-2) before tripling off the wall in center field.

Nick Frasso came out of the Rockies bullpen, but Dingler hit his first pitch over the Tigers' bullpen in left field for a 4-1 lead. It was his 27th homer, and first since Aug. 6.

Frasso then hit Clark, who stole second and scored Detroit's fifth run on a pair of wild pitches.

Greene added an RBI double in the eighth to make it 6-1. Zac Veen made it a four-run game with a ninth-inning RBI single.

The teams play the second game of their weekend series on Saturday, with Detroit throwing a bullpen game against RHP Tanner Gordon (1-4, 5.40 ERA).

title: Their fathers died on 9/11. Baseball became part of their healing
description: Twenty-five years after tragedy reshaped their lives, Brielle Saracini and Sean McGuire are showing how baseball and love can create moments of joy in the shadow of unimaginable loss.
fullText:
NEW YORK — How can pain and joy, love and heartbreak, coexist, side by side, year after year? How could the worst day of your life lead to the best? How do you rebuild a life shattered in an instant?

One ballgame at a time, as it turns out.

On Friday night, the 25th anniversary of 9/11, Brielle Saracini and her husband Sean McGuire provided the highlight of an emotional pregame ceremony when they threw out the game's ceremonial first pitch at Yankee Stadium. Both 37, they represent both the tragedy and the resolve of 9/11, the devastation of loss and the strength of resilience. Brielle's father Victor was the captain of United Flight 175, the plane which impacted the South Tower … where Sean's father, Patrick, worked on the 84th floor.

The two were just 10 years old when their fathers died. They met two years later at Camp Better Days, a camp established to help children who had lost a parent on 9/11, and were married on Sept. 9, 2017. And on Friday night, they walked out on the field together — Brielle wearing a Derek Jeter jersey, Sean bravely wearing a Mike Piazza Mets one — showing that joy can come from even the most horrifying of days.

Brielle Saracini and Sean McGuire share a special moment in the Bronx.

As kids, they both lost their fathers on 9/11. They met in 2003, became friends first, then fell in love.

They married in 2017.

Yankees legends from 2001 - including Hall of Famers Derek Jeter, Mariano… pic.twitter.com/oVSXorzkSK

"You're so happy and thankful for so many things that have come your way after 9/11," Brielle said a few minutes after her pitch. "But it comes at a terrible price."

Friday morning dawned in New York the same way that Tuesday did 25 years ago, with a brilliant blue sky that seemed to go on forever. And much like the first hours of that terrible day, everything felt normal. All over the city, New Yorkers hustled down streets and up avenues in a typical morning rush as taxi drivers leaned on their horns. People had places to be, and not enough time to get there.

In Lower Manhattan, though, a more solemn air prevailed. At the traditional 9/11 memorial ceremony, four presidents, several mayors and thousands of still-grieving family members gathered to remember the nearly 3,000 lost on 9/11, and the hundreds more lost as a result of the attacks in the years since.

The ceremony illustrated the deep, painful and often contradictory hold that 9/11 still has on New York. Sporting blue-and-white ribbons, some family members used the occasion to speak about their loved ones, holding onto now-fading memories. Others opted to vent frustrations or demand action from the assembled politicians. And still others, in true New York fashion, thanked their departed loved ones for whatever role they had in making Knicks In Five a reality earlier this year.

The 2026 Yankees have spent the last few weeks leading up to September 11 in much the same way the 2001 team did, though without the searing pain of immediate tragedy. Manager Aaron Boone, Aaron Judge, Cam Schlitter and others visited four fire stations in Manhattan, both to express gratitude and to understand a bit more about a moment that, for many of them, is only history.

"I talked to our players a little bit about [9/11], because everyone has a different context," Boone said Friday afternoon. "Some of our guys weren't born."

That's a growing challenge for those who lived through 9/11, to communicate the meaning and importance of it to a nation that, increasingly, has no meaningful connection to that day. Almost 40 percent of Americans now are too young to remember 9/11, too young to remember the fear and the horror that consumed the entire country, too young to remember the terror that quickly gave way to unity and resolve. As fractured as the nation is right now, it's worth remembering that it wasn't always this way … and that baseball had a small role in the healing process.

"As an athlete, it was the first time that I said to myself, 'Why am I even playing?'" Derek Jeter said Friday evening. "My initial thought was, 'We're not going to come back. What does baseball mean?' And then you had a chance to meet a lot of family members who lost loved ones … and that's when you realize that our job was to at least try to give people something to cheer for for a few hours a day."

One of those family members Jeter met was Brielle, who wrote The Captain a letter just three days after her father died. Jeter eventually got the letter and quickly invited Brielle and her family to batting practice.

"When we invited her to the stadium, you really don't know what to say," Jeter said. "You know, I don't even know if I said 'I'm sorry' or anything like that. I just tried to make her day feel special."

He did that day, introducing her to several Yankees, and he did for years afterward, offering friendship and encouragement even as she navigated a life without a father.

"It was just an incredible display of kindness — in a time where we all just felt the gravity of the situation that was rooted in hate, to be able to then flip that around and find a bright spot," Brielle said, adding, "It became this special thing that healed me. It healed 10-year-old Brielle."

Baseball can't dull the pain of tragedy or bring back a loved one. But baseball can bring a bit of normalcy to a tragic time. After 9/11, that's exactly what New York needed, and on Friday night New York tapped back into that feeling.

Bruce Springsteen's "The Rising," the defiant anthem released shortly after 9/11, began the ceremony, followed by videos documenting the 2001 Yankees' inspiring World Series run. (They lost the series in seven to the Diamondbacks, but won all three New York games, two in dramatic extra innings.) The highlight, of course: President George W. Bush striding out of the Yankee dugout to throw a perfect strike before Game 3.

Bush wasn't in attendance Friday night, but several of those 2001 Yankees were, including Jeter, former manager Joe Torre, Mariano Rivera and Paul O'Neill. They walked out to thunderous applause, and then it was time for Brielle and Sean to take the stage.

Sean's pitch reached "catcher" Paul Goldschmidt, but Brielle, throwing to Cody Bellinger, bounced hers, much to her horror.

"He was in my head," Brielle said, nodding to Jeter. "'Don't bounce it, they'll boo you!' And then I bounced it." (For the record, no one booed her.)

The national memory of 9/11 may fade with time, but for so many — starting with the 3,051 children who lost parents in the World Trade Center attacks — the scars won't ever fade. The holes where the Twin Towers once stood remain in Lower Manhattan, a testament to what was lost. The painful absences always loom, too — missed birthdays, graduations, weddings, and yes, Yankees games.

"I never know what I want to do on each anniversary. I never know the proper way to honor my father," Brielle said as the Yankees and Mets started their game. "This feels really special. I know he'd be so proud of me. I only cried like six times today, this morning. So to balance it out with smiles, and laughs, and just overwhelming feelings of gratitude and everything, is a beautiful display of how the last 25 years have been."

title: Why Will Anderson Jr.’s ‘AFC Championship’ Framing Sets the Standard for Texans’ Week 1 Clash vs. Bills
description: Will Anderson Jr. ignites a high-stakes opener against Josh Allen, challenging Houston to treat this September heavyweight clash as a litmus test for their championship aspirations.
fullText:
The standard in H-Town is no longer just making the playoffs, but rather it is breaking through the ceiling.

As the Houston Texans put the finishing touches on their game plan for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Buffalo Bills at Reliant Stadium, star edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. set the tone Thursday, framing the Week 1 slate with unvarnished clarity.

"This is an AFC Championship matchup," Anderson told reporters outside the locker room. "Two really good teams. We have a ton of respect for them."

Calling a September kickoff a conference championship game might sound like hyperbole in most cities, but in Houston, it is an accurate reflection of where DeMeco Ryans' program stands. Coming off three consecutive postseason appearances that ended in the Divisional Round, the Texans aren't easing into 2026. They are walking straight into a litmus test against a perennial AFC powerhouse.

Will Anderson Jr. on the matchup with the Bills:

“This is an AFC Championship matchup. Two really good teams, we got a ton of respect for them. Josh Allen leading the way. Really great offensive line. James Cook, the best running back in the league— one of the best running backs… pic.twitter.com/7hYGLotGtc

Why does a Week 1 game carry this much weight? Because history and chemistry demands it.

This marks the third consecutive season the Bills have traveled to Reliant Stadium. Houston won both previous meetings: a walk-off field goal victory in 2024 and a physical four-point win in 2025 where Matt Burke's defense tormented Josh Allen with eight sacks.

Yet, as the Texans launch their 2026 campaign, the landscape on both sides of the ball presents fresh variables that make this opener critical.

On defense, Anderson enters the season as a top contender for NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Paired alongside Danielle Hunter, the tandem represents one of the most disruptive pass-rushing duos in football. Against an off-script playmaker like Allen, the ability to generate edge pressure without blitzing is the exact formula Houston relied on last fall.

Offensively, all eyes are on how C.J. Stroud establishes rhythm amid a restructured receiving corps. With Tank Dell beginning the year on injured reserve and sophomore receiver Jayden Higgins lost to a camp ACL tear, Houston's passing attack will rely heavily on Nico Collins, newly acquired trade target Kayshon Boutte, and second-year slot weapon Jaylin Noel.

The addition of veteran back David Montgomery behind Pro Bowl guard Wyatt Teller and first-round rookie guard Keylan Rutledge gives Houston an identity built for physical, grind-it-out football. That ground game will be vital for controlling the clock and limiting Allen's extra possessions.

Anderson's mindset highlights a fundamental shift in the franchise's culture. The Texans aren't treating Week 1 as an experimental dress rehearsal. They view it as a direct statement to the rest of the conference.

For fantasy managers, expect heavy target volume for Nico Collins and a steady workload for Montgomery in 12-personnel packages. For die-hard fans, Sunday is a early barometer of whether Houston's upgraded trenches can vault them past the Divisional Round glass ceiling.

title: Tigers’ late-season rotation shuffle is giving them an early look at 2027
description: Detroit evaluates Andrew Sears and Jackson Jobe while monitoring Jack Flaherty’s recovery, using September’s roster flux to audition high-velocity arms for a future championship pitching staff.
fullText:
The rotation for the Detroit Tigers for the rest of the month is shaping up

The Detroit Tigers are out of the postseason race, but the final weeks of the season are still giving them something useful: opportunities to evaluate how several pitchers might fit into the 2027 rotation.

That became even more apparent Friday with another round of rotation news. Left-hander Andrew Sears is expected to start Saturday against Colorado while Keider Montero heads to Venezuela for the birth of his child. Jack Flaherty, meanwhile, is scheduled to throw a two-to-three inning simulated game Saturday as he continues working back from right forearm flexor inflammation. River Ryan has also started his buildup at Triple-A Toledo, while Jackson Jobe is scheduled to start Sunday against the Rockies.

For a team already looking toward next year, that is a lot of moving pieces worth watching.

Sears is the most immediate one. He has already shown some value in a small major league sample, including 5 2/3 innings of one-run ball against Cleveland on Sept. 4. His fastball is not overpowering compared to some of Detroit's other young arms, but he has shown enough strike-throwing ability and secondary stuff to make these September innings meaningful. Saturday gives the Tigers another chance to see whether he can be more than emergency depth.

Montero's situation is different. He has already thrown 147 innings this season and has spent much of the year in the rotation, posting a 3.55 ERA. His workload is near his career high, so moving him aside temporarily while he goes on paternity leave also gives Detroit a natural opportunity to look at someone else. There has also been some suggestion that Montero could work out of the bullpen once Flaherty returns, which adds another layer to how the Tigers may use him down the stretch.

Flaherty may be the most important health question of the group. He has been out since late July with flexor inflammation and threw only 19 pitches in his first rehab outing. Saturday's simulated game should stretch him out a little more, and if that goes well, he could return to Detroit's rotation sometime next week. The key at this point is less about results and more about whether he finishes the season healthy enough to enter the offseason without another setback.

Then there is River Ryan, who might be the most intriguing long-term piece. In his first outing with Toledo, Ryan threw two scoreless innings, allowed two soft hits and struck out two. His fastball averaged 97 mph and topped out at 98.2, while his slider averaged 91.7 mph. That is encouraging considering he is working his way back from both Tommy John surgery and a hamstring issue. Detroit has not ruled out giving him major league innings before the season ends.

Jobe is already getting those innings. He is scheduled to start Sunday and remains one of the more important arms in the organization despite the uneven results that come with returning from major surgery. His last outing in Cleveland included seven strikeouts over five innings, matching his career high, and every start now gives Detroit another data point heading into 2027.

The Tigers are not going to answer every rotation question in September, but they can start narrowing the list. Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Jobe, Montero, Flaherty, Ryan and Sears all bring different levels of certainty, experience and health risk. The final two weeks are less about finding a perfect five-man rotation and more about figuring out which arms deserve to be part of that conversation when spring training begins.

For a team no longer playing meaningful games in the standings, that evaluation may be one of the more useful things left to accomplish.

title: Rams’ disastrous performance against 49ers featured one jarring surprise, says analyst
description: The Los Angeles Rams didn't look like a Super Bowl contender in their season opener.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams didn't look like a Super Bowl contender in their season opener.

The Rams, who were dubbed as the favorites to hoist the Lombardi Trophy at the end of the season, looked mediocre in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers.

Head coach Sean McVay was out-coached. Quarterback Matthew Stafford played poorly. Reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was nowhere to be found, recording zeros across the board in his Rams debut.

And Aaron Donald was watching the Australia showdown from LA.

The result? The 49ers handed the Super Bowl favorites a 27-7 beatdown in their season opener.

NFL analyst Danny Parkins shared what surprised him the most about the Rams' lackluster performance Thursday.

"I think the most surprising thing about the whole thing is seven points. The Rams scored seven points in a football game," Parkins said on First Things First.

"I just could not stop thinking about the ineptitude of the Rams offense."

What surprised you most about last night's game? @DannyParkins answers:

“7 points. 7 points! The Rams scored 7 points in a football game!” pic.twitter.com/Tirt6UFFcS

It was the Rams' largest loss in 38 games. It was the fewest points scored in a Stafford start in 84 games. Stafford posted the lowest passer rating he's had in 70 games and it was the first time in 18 games that he recorded zero touchdowns.

The notion that Week 1 lies remains true, but the Rams certainly didn't set the tone for what was poised to be an electric season with their disappointing performance in Melbourne.

title: Raheem Morris, I Wasn't Familiar With Your Game: Inside the 49ers' Masterclass Defense
description: Schematic brilliance and pre-snap disguises dismantled Sean McVay’s offense as San Francisco stifled Matthew Stafford, proving that tactical discipline outweighs raw pressure in high-stakes defensive domination.
fullText:
Coming into the season opener at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, all eyes were on how the San Francisco 49ers defense would manage the pass rush with Nick Bosa on a rotational snap budget (he ended up playing the entire game) and front-line depth depleted by injuries. But defensive coordinator Raheem Morris delivered an absolute masterclass in scheme execution, leading the 49ers to a dominant 27-7 victory over the Los Angeles Rams. While San Francisco didn't generate overwhelming pressure off the line of scrimmage, Morris had Sean McVay's high-powered attack completely solved from the opening whistle.

Rather than relying on raw pass-rush wins to rattle reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, Morris relied on schematic discipline, pre-snap disguises, and layered zones.

The 49ers took away the intermediate middle of the field, forcing Stafford into hesitant, late read checkdowns and contested boundary throws. Stafford was held to just 155 passing yards and spent the last three quarters completely shut down, managing only four completions in the first half as San Francisco erased Los Angeles' quick game rhythm.

Morris' defensive masterwork was capped by two defining situational stops:

The Goal-Line Wall: Late in the third quarter, holding a ten point lead, the Rams drove to the 49ers' 1-yard line. On fourth-and-goal, Stafford attempted a QB sneak, but Morris' front held the line, with Osa Odighizuwa and Keion White stonewalling the attempt for a massive turnover on downs.

Secondary Traps: Cornerback Renardo Green executed a flawless zone read early in the game, jumping a route for a leaping interception that set the tone for the secondary.

Later in the fourth quarter, All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner delivered the knockout blow, punching the ball loose from tight end Tyler Higbee to kill another Rams drive and preserve the double digit lead.

With Bosa's snaps carefully budgeted and new interior pieces integrating on the fly, Morris proved that elite defensive calling isn't always about blitzing high or generating backfield chaos. It's about taking away what the opponent does best, executing in critical high leverage moments, and dictating the tempo of the game.

title: “No One’s Coming to Save You”: Michigan Great Delivers Brutal Reality Check to Bryce Underwood Amid Questions About His Future
description: Michigan football fans expected a dominant kickoff to the season, but instead, they got a massive scare against an FBS opponent. The Wolverines barely scraped by Western Michigan with a controversial 13-12 win, leaving a trail of questions about their highly touted quarterback, Bryce Underwood.
fullText:
Michigan football fans expected a dominant kickoff to the season, but instead, they got a massive scare against an FBS opponent. The Wolverines barely scraped by Western Michigan with a controversial 13-12 win, leaving a trail of questions about their highly touted quarterback, Bryce Underwood. With a high-stakes matchup against the No. 11 Oklahoma Sooners looming at the Big House, former Michigan All-American left tackle Taylor Lewan decided it was time to step in with some unfiltered truths.

Speaking on a recent panel alongside Will Compton and Josh Pate, Lewan did not sugarcoat the situation. He noted that the young quarterback is dealing with a brand-new kind of spotlight, one fueled by a monstrous $12 million NIL package and immediate expectations to be perfect. After a week of endless internet critiques, Lewan laid out the ultimate football reality on ESPN College Football:

"The whole world wants this kid to fail this week because there may or may not have been a second on the clock, and there must be justice for another Michigan team in this state," the former Wolverines lineman said (via @ESPNCFB on X). "So if I'm in his camp, I'm sitting there and saying, 'Listen to it, digest it, and understand. This is the real world right now. You get paid a lot of money. There's a lot of expectation on you, and if you don't perform, the worst thing is going to happen. He needs to run the football as much as possible. He needs to protect the football when he's throwing it."

For Lewan, the biggest hurdle for the young signal-caller isn't just the opposing defense. It's the invisible weight holding him back on the field.

Michigan football's ups and downs are worth following closely. 

The former offensive lineman believes the program needs to stop shielding its young star if they expect him to grow. He explained that the team has to let the player be free, make mistakes, and handle the pressure head-on.

"But more than anything, he needs to let the guardrails off of himself. He needs to go out there and live and die by the sword. But more than anything, he has to understand something you and I say to each other every time there's adversity striking one of our lives: no one's coming to save you. You can only save yourself. I'm there with him. I'll be sitting there on Saturday and rooting for the kid. I want him to be successful, and I believe he still can be that guy. But truly, it's a do-or-die situation for him."

The majority of Wolverine fans cut him some slack last season because he had no QB coach to guide him. One of the first things Kyle Whittingham did when he arrived in Ann Arbor was to hook him up with Jason Bateman and a QB coach while promising to run the offense to the best of his abilities.

Despite all that offseason work, the debut of the Underwood-Whittingham era turned into a rollercoaster. The former five-star QB completed just 54.5% of his passes for 170 yards, with one touchdown and one interception, while adding 47 yards and a score on the ground. The game only ended in a victory because of a chaotic, last-second 47-yard Hail Mary pass to JJ Buchanan. Because the final whistle was muddled by a stadium clock controversy, fans and rival analysts across the country have been loudly calling out the offense's stagnation.

Now, the stage is set for what many are calling the biggest game of Underwood's young life because of the stakes involved in his role in Ann Arbor. Head coach Kyle Whittingham has already hinted to the media that the starting job isn't guaranteed forever.

Rumors are swirling because backup Tommy Carr has suddenly been taking 20 percent of his practice time with the first-team offense. If the starting offense continues to sputter in the first half against Oklahoma, the staff might pivot to Carr to spark a change.

Compounding the drama is Oklahoma's notoriously aggressive, exotic defense under Brent Venables.

The Sooners were a brick wall last week, pitching a massive 51-0 shutout against UTEP. They completely suffocated the Miners, giving up a microscopic 198 total yards and grounding the passing game to just 86 yards. The Sooners lived in the backfield all night long, racking up four sacks and 10 tackles for loss, while forcing two fumbles.

Mind you, Underwood struggled heavily on the move last week, going just 2-of-8, throwing outside the numbers when pressured. To survive this weekend, analysts suggest Michigan must completely reopen the playbook, lean heavily into Underwood's elite running ability, and let him use his natural athleticism to extend plays.

Everyone in Ann Arbor wants to see the former top recruit succeed, but top-tier college football waits for no one. If Underwood wants to quiet the critics and keep hold of the starting job, he has to be the one to orchestrate the turnaround, as Lewan highlighted.

title: Texans Place Rookie DT Kayden McDonald on IR
description: The rookie second-round pick will miss at least the first four games after suffering an ankle injury during practice.
fullText:
On the eve of their regular season debut, the Houston Texans have announced another significant injury. Rookie DT Kayden McDonald is apparently suffering from an ankle injury and will begin the regular season on injured reserve. Battle Red Blog's Nickschwager noted McDonald's appearance on the injury report yesterday, but a placement on IR is a new and rather sudden development.

The Texans have placed Kayden McDonald on IR & signed Jaden Crumedy to the 53 man roster in a corresponding move. pic.twitter.com/JoE7xhOz1y

McDonald will now be inactive for the first four games of the 2026 regular season: vs. Buffalo Bills, vs. Cincinnati Bengals, @ Indianapolis Colts, and vs. Dallas Cowboys. He will be eligible to return for Houston's match against the Tennessee Titans on October 11th. In the meantime, the Texans are signing DT Jaden Crumedy from the Green Bay Packers practice squad.

Panthers draft Miss St DL Jaden Crumedy

 pic.twitter.com/YbiRio1op0

Houston Chronicle reporter Jonathan M. Alexander stated following the announcement, "McDonald suffered the injury in practice Wednesday, a league source said. He did not practice Thursday or Friday and wore a protective boot over his foot in the locker room"

Kayden McDonald, despite being a rookie second-round pick, was fixing to have a significant impact on Houston's dominant defensive line. He earned first team All-American honors while starting for Ohio State in 2025, and quickly ascended draft boards after establishing himself as one of the best run-stoppers in the 2026 NFL Draft. He had a lot of fans here at Battle Red Blog, and I even got the chance to ask him a question representing the Blog at the 2026 NFL Draft in Pittsburgh:

Our very own @FizzyJoe got to ask a question of the Houston #Texans' latest addition to the defense!

Here's Joe Critz with Kayden McDonald. pic.twitter.com/LXoOkmAXKl

He finished his final collegiate season with 65(!) tackles, a preposterous stat for a beefy interior lineman, and his pass-rush seemed to be improving down the stretch. Fortunately for the Texans, they still have depth in the interior defensive line, with starting DTs Sheldon Rankins and Tommy Togiai still expected to absorb the majority of snaps. But, McDonald was brought in with the express purpose of being a run-stuffer who would contribute on early downs, something that could have pushed this defense to even greater heights. And, don't look now, but there are currently four Texans defensive linemen on IR: McDonald, DE Dylan Horton, DE Solomon Byrd, and DE Ali Gaye. Fortunately, none of these players are starters, but depth at a pretty important spot on this year's Texans team is now significantly thinner, especially during a fairly grizzly opening slate of games. We already know the Cowboys and Bills have great offenses, but the Bengals and Colts could both find themselves near to the top of the league in offensive production by year's end, too.

#Texans rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald is expected to return this season, per a league source, from an ankle injury he suffered in practice.
A second-round draft pick from Ohio State and a former Big Ten Conference Defensive Lineman of the Year, McDonald can be… pic.twitter.com/kSzdhbxVCx

Regardless, this Texans defense is one of the few groups in the league that can push through this wave of injuries relatively unscathed. Togiai, Mario Edwards Jr. and free-agent addition DT Logan Hall will have bigger roles this Sunday trying to contain defending NFL rushing leader RB James Cook, who ran for 116 yards and a touchdown at a piercing 6.8 Y/A against our mighty Texans defense in Week 12 last year. They're hands will be very, very full this coming Sunday, but if there was a team able to take this blow and keep charging forward, it's this Texans team!

What do you think of this news? Are the Texans in more danger of losing their first game of the season because of this injury, or was McDonald just going to play a small role? Will new DT Jaden Crumedy surprise us all and make some sweet tackles in Week 1, or will Logan Hall have a banner game to start his Texans tenure? Let us know your thoughts down in the comments below!

title: Micah Nori Must Build a Coaching Staff That Disagrees With Him
description: Portland’s success hinges on intellectual friction. By assembling diverse perspectives to challenge his schemes, Micah Nori can preempt tactical errors and maximize a versatile, young Trail Blazers roster.
fullText:
The Portland Trail Blazers did not need Micah Nori to fill his first coaching staff with people who will simply nod along with every decision. A new head coach needs trust around him, but trust does not mean agreement. Portland needs assistants who are comfortable challenging an idea before it becomes a bad matchup, an unclear rotation or a late-game mistake that could have been avoided.

That is why the additions of Jay Triano and Mike Williams matter, while Quinton Crawford, Gilbert Abraham and the rest of the returning staff should remain valuable voices. Each coach brings a different background, perspective and relationship with the roster. Nori should use that variety as an advantage instead of trying to make every person in the room think exactly like he does.

The best coaching staffs are not quiet when a difficult decision arrives. They debate the matchup, discuss the numbers, consider the players' confidence and make sure the head coach has heard every important perspective. Once a decision is made, everybody needs to support it, but the conversation beforehand should be honest enough to identify a potential problem before the opponent exposes it.

Portland will need that kind of preparation because this roster does not fit into one simple formula. Ja Morant, Damian Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson each bring different ball-handling abilities, which means there will be nights when the right answer depends on pace, defense and who is playing well. Donovan Clingan, Robert Williams III, Yang Hansen and Branden Carlson also give Nori several big-man options with very different strengths.

No assistant should be expected to publicly undermine the head coach or create unnecessary tension. The goal is not conflict for the sake of conflict. The goal is a staff where Triano can suggest another late-game action, Williams can question a matchup, Crawford can advocate for a younger player and Nori can make a better-informed decision because he heard them out.

That approach could become especially important when the season becomes difficult. A 50-win-caliber team cannot wait for a losing streak to recognize that a lineup is not working or that a player needs clearer responsibilities. Portland must be proactive, and that begins long before tipoff inside the coaches' meeting room.

Nori will ultimately be responsible for every major decision. That is part of being the head coach. However, the Trail Blazers will be stronger if he builds an environment where the people around him are confident enough to disagree, prepared enough to explain why and united enough to move forward once the final call is made. One non-yes-man is Lillard. His impact should be helpful for Nori's transition from assistant to full-time head coach.

title: No. 18 FSU soccer ties NC State 2-2 in ACC opener
description: No. 18 Florida State hosted NC State Friday evening in its first ACC matchup of the season, ending the night with a 2-2 draw. The Seminoles move to 4-1-2 on the season, while the Wolfpack move to 7-0-2. FSU goalkeeper Kate Ockene entered the matchup after being named ACC Goalkeeper of the Week for her […]
fullText:
No. 18 Florida State hosted NC State Friday evening in its first ACC matchup of the season, ending the night with a 2-2 draw.

The Seminoles move to 4-1-2 on the season, while the Wolfpack move to 7-0-2.

FSU goalkeeper Kate Ockene entered the matchup after being named ACC Goalkeeper of the Week for her performance against Rice on Sunday.

Florida State's starting lineup featured Ockene in goal; Olivia Page and Claire Rain on the back line; Shaneil Buckley, Peyton McGovern, Joelle Jung and Sam Erbach in the midfield; and Nyah Rose, Tanner Strickland, Wrianna Hudson and Ryder Ajeto up front.

The Seminoles were still without Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke and Nyanya Touray, who are competing in the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup.

NC State wasted little time getting on the board. Erica Roberts scored just 1:37 into the match to give the Wolfpack an early 1-0 lead.

FSU continued looking for opportunities to answer, and the Seminoles found one in the 22nd minute. Buckley sent the ball to Hudson in front of the goal, where Hudson headed it into the net to tie the match at 1-1.

Use that height, Wri!! 😤 pic.twitter.com/W0Ah7Rrig1

The Seminoles continued looking for another opportunity before halftime. Erbach took a free kick from outside the 18-yard box that found Hudson, but her header was saved by NC State goalkeeper Riley Pickels.

At 41:42, Erbach had another opportunity, but her shot went just over the goal.

NC State entered halftime with seven shots compared to FSU's two. The physicality also started to show, with the Wolfpack recording four fouls and a yellow card, while the Seminoles had two fouls.

The Wolfpack regained the lead at 57:32 when sophomore Daisy Duda found the back of the net to make it 2-1.

Once again, the Seminoles had to find an answer.

At 64:29, Buckley stayed persistent in front of the goal and finished the opportunity, tying the match at 2-2.

What a pretty-placed shot by Prinny! 👑 pic.twitter.com/u2yRenKOdZ

Neither team was able to find the go-ahead goal, leaving FSU with a draw in its first ACC matchup of the season.

NC State finished the match with 13 shots, four on goal, while FSU recorded seven shots, five on goal. The Wolfpack also held an advantage in corner kicks, having eight and FSU having none. NC State finished with 12 fouls compared to six for Florida State.

Head coach Brian Pensky and the Seminoles now have more than a week away from competition to regroup, watch film and continue working on their chemistry as a team.

Florida State will return to ACC play on Sept. 27, traveling to Louisville for its second noon matchup of the season.

title: Trey Wingo, Bob Ley look back on hosting ‘SportsCenter’ on 9/11
description: Friday marked 25 years since the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Center, and across the sports world there were solemn remembrances as well as celebrations of the heroes that stepped up that day. Trey Wingo used the day to call up Bob Ley, with whom he hosted the 6 p.m. edition of SportsCenter…
fullText:
Friday marked 25 years since the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Center, and across the sports world there were solemn remembrances as well as celebrations of the heroes that stepped up that day.

Trey Wingo used the day to call up Bob Ley, with whom he hosted the 6 p.m. edition of SportsCenter on Tuesday, September 11, 2001, and look back on the surreal, traumatic, and life-changing day, and how they almost didn't go on with the show.

"As I'm driving into work that day I'm like, what am I even going to talk about today? What could remotely matter?" Wingo said. "I remember we got into the offices that day and everyone was sort of just thinking about what could we do, what's available, what's this. I was like, 'Hey maybe we should just turn over all of our resources to ABC News, give them everything.'"

Wingo remembered a meeting with Ley and producer Norby Williamson, where they discussed whether or not the show should air that night.

"I was like, I don't think we should do a show. I think it would be disrespectful. All this stuff. Because I was overwhelmed," Wingo said.

Ley was on the other side of the debate.

"I remember you sat dawn and said 'Look, here's what I think. Obviously this is a really traumatic day and we don't know what's going on, but our job as the show of record' — which is what we thought that the six o'clock SportsCenter was at that time, it was the show of record of what was going on in sports that day — you said, 'We need to chronicle this so people can understand, and have a benchmark to know what happened on that day.'"

Wingo concluded by admitting that Ley, and ultimately SportsCenter, made the right call to go on air.

"In hindsight, I was 100% wrong and you were 100% right."

From there, Ley and Wingo continue to share memories from the day itself and the days that followed, both confronting the strangeness that comes with watching something so visceral slowly become a piece of history.

They also remembered the sports moments that brought the country together in the aftermath of the attacks, namely President Bush's first pitch at Yankee Stadium and Mike Piazza's monster home run for the Mets.

title: OSU Alum Kirk Herbstreit Gets Emotional on Full-Circle Moment 20 Years After Calling Ohio State-Texas Classic
description: Kirk Herbstreit has called the biggest games in college football history. He has sat in the booth for national championships, bitter rivalries, and playoff thrillers.
fullText:
Kirk Herbstreit has called the biggest games in college football history. He has sat in the booth for national championships, bitter rivalries, and playoff thrillers. Yet, certain games stay locked in his heart forever. Returning to Austin to call Ohio State against Texas is not just another assignment for him. It is a deeply personal walk down memory lane.

More than twenty years after Kirk Herbstreit called the 2005 Ohio State-Texas classic with Brent Musburger, he is walking back into Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium Saturday night to call the same matchup again. This time, Chris Fowler will be beside him. The OSU alum shared a clip from that 2005 broadcast on Instagram, and you could hear the memories coming through the caption.

"21 years ago almost to the day, #1 Ohio State @ #2 Texas met in week two of Saturday Night Football on ABC's debut season. Brent Musburger and I called the game and 21 years later… I'm calling the same matchup with @chrisfowler tomorrow night! Enjoy this flash from the past… Excited to see this matchup again soon!"

In 2005, Kirk Herbstreit was still building his broadcasting career. Ohio State arrived in Austin ranked No. 1, Texas was No. 2, and Vince Young was becoming one of the most dangerous players in the country. Troy Smith was running the Buckeyes' offense. Texas eventually won 25-22, finishing the night with a late touchdown that turned an already enormous game into a classic.

Ohio State and Texas have a way of delivering the biggest moments in college football. 

Kirk Herbstreit got another crack at the matchup a year later. Ohio State won that one 24-7 in Columbus. But maybe it's not the scoreboard that he remembers the most. Before that 2006 meeting, he was stunned by the number of Ohio State fans expected to make the trip to Texas.

Estimates reached 30,000 to 40,000 Buckeye fans, an absurd traveling crowd for a regular-season nonconference game at the time. Kirk Herbstreit also had a soft spot for those fans who packed their bags and followed Ohio State across the country.

"My favorite fans of Ohio State are those that go on the road," he said.

Two decades later, that traveling Buckeye army remains part of the show. And the game itself has somehow gotten even bigger. No. 1 Ohio State and No. 4 Texas meet Saturday night with both teams sitting at 1-0. This is the big one in the Big Ten-SEC showdown, with the two programs meeting again after two Buckeye wins.

That 2005 broadcast was the launchpad that turned Herbstreit from a promising young analyst into the undisputed voice of college football. Returning to the exact same press box two decades later carries immense personal weight, but the stakes on the field are just as massive.

With top-five rankings on the line and early College Football Playoff positioning hanging in the balance, this top-tier Big Ten SEC battle gives him the ultimate stage to celebrate how far both his career and this iconic national rivalry have come.

Ohio State took the last two, winning 28-14 in the CFP semifinal in the Cotton Bowl after the 2024 season. Then again, they beat Texas 14-7 in Columbus to start last season. Now Texas gets another shot, this time in Austin. The details are enough to make this one of the season's biggest games. Will Muschamp is taking over the Longhorns' defense, while Arthur Smith enters his first season directing the Buckeyes' offense.

There is no shortage of star power. Julian Sayin and Arch Manning headline the QB matchup. Jeremiah Smith remains the obvious problem for the Longhorns, although Texas has managed to handle him in the last two meetings. The Buckeye WR caught one pass for three yards in the playoff and six for 43 yards last season.

For Kirk Herbstreit, though, there is another layer. He was there when Ohio State-Texas first became appointment television. He watched thousands of Buckeye fans flood Austin. He has spent the years since becoming one of the most familiar voices in college football. Now he gets to call the matchup again inside the same stadium with the same two powerhouses. And that is what makes his full-circle moment feel a little bigger than just another Saturday night.

title: Tampa Bay Rays first to clinch MLB playoff berth on Junior Caminero walk-off homer
description: The Tampa Bay Rays are the first team to lock up a spot in the 2026 MLB playoffs. They did it in dramatic fashion.
fullText:
The Tampa Bay Rays became the first major league club to clinch a 2026 playoff berth - and they did so in walk-off fashion thanks to their superstar third baseman.

Junior Caminero hit his 40th home run of the season, a two-run shot off Houston Astros reliever Bryan Abreu, and the Rays punched their postseason ticket in the giddiest fashion possible, beating the Astros 3-1 Friday, Sept. 11 at Tropicana Field.

The Rays (88-59) return to the postseason for the first time since 2023, when they won 99 games but were eliminated by the eventual champion Texas Rangers in the wild-card round.

This season, their sights are set much higher.

The Rays retain a three-game lead over the New York Yankees in the American League East, and the division champion is nearly assured the top seed in the AL and a first-round bye. Tampa Bay entered Friday with an 81% chance to win the divison, according to FanGraphs.

Jonathan Aranda nearly ended it a batter earlier, when his shot to right center field hit just below the yellow line on the outfield fence. He settled for a one-out double. Caminero then leaned back and blasted an Abreu first-pitch fastball 417 feet over the wall in left, his AL-leading 40th of the season.

JUNIOR CAMINERO WALKS IT OFF@RAYSBASEBALL HEADS TO THE POSTSEASON! pic.twitter.com/tkDpYi0OEe

Caminero pounded his chest twice, exhorted his teammates in the Rays dugout and commenced a joyous trip around the bases as Tropicana Field roared.

That culminated a crisp ballgame in which starter Drew Rasmussen pitched seven innings of one-run ball. Closer Bryan Baker pitched a scoreless ninth to earn the win.

Tampa Bay has the AL's best record for a reason, a club with one legitimate superstar in third baseman Caminero and a slew of well-fitting parts. The Rays lineup is a daunting combination of power and speed, with Caminero's AL-leading 40 home runs tucked in the lineup around slugger Yandy Díaz (22 homers, .835 OPS) and first baseman Aranda (19 homers, .359 OBP). Speedy Chandler Simpson ranks second in the AL with a .306 average and the club makes contact better than any team in the majors.

Meanwhile, right-handers Nick Martinez and Rasmussen have combined for a 28-5 record and ERAs of 2.92 and 2.81, respectively.

Tampa Bay has two games remaining with the Astros before hosting the Athletics for three games. And then the road gets tougher to finish the season.

The Rays host third-place Boston for three games before a challenging seven-game road trip, beginning with four games at Yankee Stadium Sept. 22-24 that should go a long way toward determining the division title. Tampa Bay finishes the regular season with three games at NL wild-card hopeful Philadelphia.

If the Rays hold on and win the division, they will play host to Game 1 of the five-game AL Division Series on Saturday, Oct. 3.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Tampa Bay Rays first to clinch MLB playoff berth on Junior Caminero walk-off homer

title: Rays become first team to clinch playoff spot this season on Caminero's walk-off homer
description: Junior Caminero sent the Tampa Bay Rays to the playoffs.  The Rays became the first major league team to secure a postseason spot, beating the Houston Astros 3-1 Friday night on Caminero's game-ending, two-run homer — his 40th of the season.  Tampa Bay (88-59) has held the American League's best record for 115 days this season.
fullText:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Junior Caminero sent the Tampa Bay Rays to the playoffs.

The Rays became the first major league team to secure a postseason spot, beating the Houston Astros 3-1 Friday night on Caminero's game-ending, two-run homer — his 40th of the season.

Tampa Bay (88-59) has held the American League's best record for 115 days this season. The Rays began Friday with a three-game lead over the New York Yankees in the AL East. The next goals for Tampa Bay are securing the division title and then locking up the AL's best record and a first-round playoff bye.

It's the first playoff berth in three seasons for the Rays, who lost both games to Texas in a wild-card series in 2023.

The Rays locked up a postseason spot earlier than any team since the Atlanta Braves did it on Sept. 10, 2023, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.

However, among the clubs that were first to secure playoff berths over the previous 10 seasons, only the Chicago Cubs (2016), Boston Red Sox (2018), Los Angeles Dodgers (2020) and New York Yankees (2024) have reached the World Series.

title: The talking's over: Garcia and Benn make weight for Saturday's title fight
description: From a hard-boiled egg to a warning about a father's safety, Garcia and Benn's fight week reached its breaking point before either man ever stepped in the ring.
fullText:
LAS VEGAS — All the talking is done. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn both made weight Friday morning at Meta Apex, and by Saturday night at T-Mobile Arena, the only thing left to settle is who walks out with the WBC welterweight title.

Getting there took a full week of noise, and Thursday's final press conference at T-Mobile Arena delivered as much of it as any single moment all week. Fans were lined up outside the arena well before doors opened, with a separate media check-in line running alongside them and a real buzz building in the plaza. Once everyone settled into the air-conditioned arena, Dana White opened the floor, and the first question went straight at Garcia: why he skipped Tuesday's scheduled face-off. He gave the same answer he'd given all week. He has a routine during fight week, and he didn't feel it was necessary to be there.

Ryan Garcia responds to a question during Thursday's press conference at T-Mobile Arena.

Asked next whether he thought he was getting under Benn's skin, Garcia set the microphone down, reached into his bag, and cracked a hard-boiled egg on the table. Whether it was intentional or not, the moment was hard to separate from history. Chris Eubank Jr. slapped Benn in the face with an egg at a press conference last year, mocking the contaminated-egg explanation floated for one of Benn's failed drug tests. That stunt cost Eubank Jr. a six-figure fine. Garcia didn't wait to finish chewing before he started answering. He mumbled through a mouthful of egg with the mic still sitting on the table, making the point that he didn't care what Benn thought without bothering to be understood, then picked the mic back up and repeated it clearly enough for everyone to hear.

Benn, for his part, brushed off questions about his own weight-making and insisted he was focused only on himself. Asked how he planned to deal with Garcia's left hook, he said he wasn't concerned, and that he brings tenacity, ferocity, spite and experience built from fighting in front of massive crowds before. When a reporter brought up Benn having questioned whether Garcia is "a real Mexican," Garcia didn't let it go. He made clear Benn had no standing to question his heritage, and that fighting during Mexican Independence Day weekend only added to what's on the line for him Saturday. He said Saturday night would settle that the same way it settles everything else.

Conor Benn speaks to the crowd with his father Nigel Benn at his side at Thursday's press conference inside the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas

There were lighter beats too. Asked about signing with Zuffa Boxing, Benn's team credited the move with making the fight possible at all. Dana White called Benn the most professional fighter he's ever worked with, and Garcia cut in mid-answer, mockingly calling him "a good boy" before Dana could finish the thought.

Ryan Garcia and Conor share some back and forth at Thursday's final press conference inside of the the T-Mobile Arena as Zuffa President Dana White looks on.

Then the room went quiet in a different way. Garcia's tone shifted, his voice dropped, and he turned to point directly at Benn and Benn's father, warning that if Benn doesn't walk out of that ring okay Saturday, it's on his dad. Benn and his father just looked forward and nodded. It was the one moment all week that didn't feel like theater.

Ryan Garcia turns directly to Conor Benn and his father as things got heated between the two welterweight fighters at Thursday's press conference

The presser closed on a surprise. Teofimo Lopez had been sitting in disguise a few feet away for most of the session before revealing himself after Garcia named him as someone he still has to beat. Benn's reaction summed up the room: "I like that."

WBA welterweight champion Teofimo Lopez reveals himself to be the media member in disguise that asked both fighters a question during Thursday afternoon's press conference.

Friday morning brought a much quieter scene. The line outside Meta Apex started forming before 8 a.m., and by 9, media had settled into the weigh-in section with the scale up on stage. Benn was up first, called out from the side stage, and stepped on the scale to a visible smile, maybe even relief, as he hit 146 pounds.

Conor Benn officially makes weight at 146 lbs. at Friday morning's weigh-in from the Meta Apex in Las Vegas

Garcia hadn't arrived yet, so the rest of the card weighed in without him. He walked in midway through, went straight to the scale, and made 145.5 with WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman looking on, just as Sulaiman had for Benn. Both fighters comfortably inside the 147-pound limit, no drama, no excuses left to make.

Ryan Garcia weighs in at 145.5 lbs. and officially makes weight for his WBC welterweight title defense against Conor Benn at the T-Mobile Arena on Saturday night in Las Vegas.

title: Rockies bullpen collapse spoils Mason Adams start in 6-2 loss to Detroit
description: Rookie relievers cough up five runs in the sixth inning
fullText:
The Colorado Rockies entered Detroit hoping to snap a seven-game losing streak on the road. Despite a solid start from their rookie pitcher and an offense that out-hit the Tigers, the Rockies bullpen collapsed in the middle innings, leading to a 6-2 defeat. They are now just eight games away from losing 100 games for the fourth season in a row.

Making his fourth big-league start, Mason Adams continued to impress in a Rockies uniform with a fairly quick and efficient outing.

The night started promisingly as Adams struck out the side in the bottom of the first inning. In the second, he allowed a leadoff single to Riley Greene and a one-out walk to Max Clark but managed to escape with a ground ball double play. He then worked a quick 1-2-3 third inning followed by a quick fourth inning where he faced the minimum.

Through the first four innings, Adams had thrown just 52 pitches with four groundouts and looked primed to go the deepest into the game than he had previously. Unfortunately, he had to labor in the fifth inning with 25 pitches.

After the Rockies had taken the lead in the top half of the fifth inning, it didn't take long for the Tigers to tie things up. After striking out Dillon Dingler for the second time, Adams surrendered a solo home run to rookie outfielder Max Clark on a fastball that was low and inside. The home run may have rattled Adams a smidge as he walked the next two batters, but he got out of the inning by inducing another double-play ball.

His night was over after 77 pitches, having allowed just the one run on two hits over five innings with five strikeouts against three walks. Adams pounded the zone and the Detroit lineup had a tough time squaring him up. Even the pitch Clark hit out was a quality offering that he just got beat on. The efficiency was on point and the future remains quite bright for the young right-hander.

"I thought [Adams] was really good," manager Warren Schaeffer said. "He got behind in some counts and had some walks but other than that I thought the breaking ball was really good. The punch-out was high; he looked sharp."

"I think it all goes back to his poise and his preparation. He looks in total control out there and he has really good stuff. Those two things combined and the presence he brings on the mound, it's something that lines up for a long time in the future."

After a great performance by the rookie starter, the Rockies turned to rookie reliever Mark Manfredi in the sixth inning. After retiring Kevin McGonigle to start the inning, Manfredi walked Gleybor Torres. He then got pinch-hitter Spencer Torkelson to fly out to right field for the second out of the inning. Riley Greene then stepped up to the plate and seemingly struck out to end the inning, but he challenged the pitch, which was flipped to a ball. Greene then launched a ball to center field that Cole Carrigg tracked all the way to the wall, but as he hit the wall and got tied up as the ball hit the wall right next to his glove. Greene ended up with an RBI triple to give the Tigers a 2-1 lead.

The Rockies then turned to rookie reliever Nick Frasso.

Unfortunately, Dingler unloaded on the first pitch he saw for a two-run home run — his first long ball in five weeks — to put the Tigers up 4-1. Frasso lost all command of his pitches as he spiked a curveball that hit Clark, who promptly stole second base. Frasso then yanked back-to-back wild pitches that allowed Clark to move up to third base and subsequently score and make it 5-1 Tigers. John Peck then walked and stole second base before Zach McKinstry flew out to finally end the inning.

Blas Castaño took over in the seventh inning and worked a quick inning, but the Tigers collected their sixth run of the game when Greene collected an RBI double in the eighth inning. He managed to escape without any further damage.

The bullpen surrendered five runs on just three hits while walking three and hitting a batter, while recording zero strikeouts.

Much like the series in New York, the Rockies had opportunities to score but couldn't put much together against Tigers starter Framber Valdez. The Rockies managed to get a pair of base runners in the first inning, but Valdez escaped with a double-play ball from Hunter Goodman.

The ground ball was quite prevalent for Valdez throughout his start. Through his six innings of work, he induced 11 groundouts while striking out just two batters and issuing two walks.

The Rockies finally managed to crack through in the fifth inning, but it took a lot of frustration. Troy Johnston led off the inning with a single and moved up to third when Jordan Beck singled to right field. With runners on the corners, Ezequiel Tovar dropped a bunt that resulted in a flip play by Valdez to cut down Johnston at the plate. Jake McCarthy then lined up a ball into right that looked like it would score Beck from second base. Unfortunately, McKinstry got to the ball quickly and fired a bullet to home plate to cut down Beck.

Connor Norby then managed to draw a walk to load the bases with two outs. Carrigg rolled over on a ball to third base that ended up kicking off the heel of McGonigle's glove, allowing Tovar to score and give the Rockies a brief 1-0 lead.

Jacob Waguespack replaced Valdez and threw two scoreless innings, giving up just one hit while striking out two. The Rockies then were able to threaten in the ninth inning against Brant Hurter. Adael Amador singled to lead off and eventually came in to score on a two-out infield single by Zac Veen. McCarthy then singled to put two runners on, his third hit of the game, which prompted Detroit to bring in Kenley Jansen. He then retired Norby on three pitches.

The Rockies lineup only had five strikeouts while out-hitting the Tigers 10-5, but they had no extra-base hits and went 2-for-8 with runners in scoring position. The lack of thump and lost chances in the fifth inning, combined with the dozen groundouts, made for another tough night offensively.

The series continues Saturday morning with Tanner Gordon (1-4, 5.40 ERA) taking the ball for the Rockies. Detroit has yet to announce a starting pitcher.

First pitch is scheduled for 11:10 am MDT.

title: 49ers news: Steve Young gives Brock Purdy props for underrated aspect of his game
description: San Francisco legend Steve Young had praises to sing about Brock Purdy following the 49ers’ opening 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia on Thursday. Despite a slow start, Brock Purdy had a great performance leading the offense. He completed 25 out of 34 passes for 205 yards and three touchdowns and one interception. He was active on the […] The post 49ers news: Steve Young gives Brock Purdy props for underrated aspect of his game appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
49ers news: Steve Young gives Brock Purdy props for underrated aspect of his game appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

San Francisco legend Steve Young had praises to sing about Brock Purdy following the 49ers' opening 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia on Thursday.

Despite a slow start, Brock Purdy had a great performance leading the offense. He completed 25 out of 34 passes for 205 yards and three touchdowns and one interception. He was active on the ground as well, racking up five rushes for 29 yards.

Young took note of the rushing aspect, discussing it in his appearance on the Rich Eisen show. Having won three Super Bowls throughout his career with the 49ers from 1987 to 1999, it is clear that Young encouraged the star quarterback to be active with his runs.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"You have to, it's the game today. It's too many free yards. Matthew Stafford is a sophisticated enough passer. He can get away with it, but no one else can. You have to be able to go get those yards, and I've encouraged Brock. 'When you break into the league, focus on the sophisticated pocket passing because that's where that's where you have to do it.' I mean, no matter how much movement you have, Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, doesn't matter who it is, you have to master that or you can't get to the Super Bowl," Young said.

"So I appreciate Brock spending the time there, but now it's like trying to expand and use those legs in unique ways. And the more it's like no, I'm not telling them 'run more, run.' I'm just saying you have to be able to do that, and he's showing that, and that's really cool."

49ers legend Steve Young breaks down the importance of Brock Purdy incorporating running in his game on the @RichEisenShow 🙌

"You have to, it's the game today. It's too many free yards." pic.twitter.com/V6Bprpf5j9

— NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) September 11, 2026

Brock Purdy and the 49ers expected a tough test, taking on a Rams squad that garnered conversations of Super Bowl contention. Following this game, it seems that San Francisco has a strong case to make as well.

Los Angeles took a 7-3 lead in the second quarter after Kyren Williams scored the first touchdown of the game. It was all San Francisco from there on, scoring 24 unanswered points to coast to victory in the Land Down Under.

Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black combined for 133 rushing yards. Meanwhile, the receiving core of Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel Sr. caught touchdown passes in the receiving game.

The 49ers will look forward to their next matchup, returning home from Australia. They host the Miami Dolphins as kickoff commences on Sept. 20 at 4:25 p.m. ET.

title: Kansas-Missouri referee Jason Autrey injured in first half of rivalry game
description: In what had already been a chaotic first half, referee Jason Autrey suffered an apparent injury in Kansas vs. Missouri game, creating some confusion.
fullText:
The matchup between Kansas and Missouri was already an insane first half before the college football contest lost one of its peacekeepers, seemingly for the rest of the game.

After Kansas returned a blocked field goal for a touchdown, the broadcast came back to show white-hat referee Jason Autrey writhing in pain on the sideline, clutching his leg. Speculation from the Fox booth indicated it may have been a pulled hamstring.

REQUIRED READING: Missouri vs Kansas football live updates: Week 2 game score, highlights

Kansas blocked a FG for a TD and destroyed the ref’s hamstring on the return pic.twitter.com/HNXflYANNL

Autrey was shown various times stretching on the sideline after the play, but was eventually carted off the field in a surreal sight.

The protocol in the aftermath of the Autrey injury was, in a word, confusing. Rules analyst Mike Pereira noted that there isn't a backup, which means there are only six officials and no white-hats on the field. The center judge took over in the backfield.

New problems arose. For starters, there wasn't a working microphone on the field after Autrey's injury, which led to the Fox booth having some fun by having Pereira announce some calls.

In a game that had already seen several blocked kicks and turnovers, not to mention one that had some serious vitriol coming in, it will be interesting to see how the absence of the lead official impacts things moving forward.
